_meta.purpose: Source data for assets/figures/throughput-box.svg. Every value below is computed by the query in this file, read-only, against Virtual Lab production CockroachDB cluster vprod. Nothing here is typed by hand or estimated.
read_before_use: CLAIMS.md is the authority on what may be published. This file records what the database SAYS.
Each respondent is assigned to ONE study per day before counting. Without that de-duplication every figure inflates by ~1.67x -- see the umbrella-group defect under C-089.
The >=20 floor is an analyst's choice and must be published as one. The figure's source line states it.

population.description: Distribution across studies, each represented by its own median active day.
population.active_day: A study-day on which at least 20 respondents were recruited.
population.recruited_on_day: The date of a respondent's first response within that study, UTC.

study_day_level.note: Lower than the per-study distribution because long slow studies contribute many days each. Not the published figure -- weight each study once.

query: WITH sc AS (SELECT DISTINCT cc.campaignid, sh AS shortcode FROM campaign_confs cc, jsonb_array_elements(cc.conf) AS s, jsonb_array_elements_text(s->'shortcodes') AS sh WHERE cc.conf_type='stratum'), old_fs AS (SELECT sc.campaignid::string AS sid, r.userid AS uid, min(r.timestamp)::date AS day FROM responses r JOIN sc ON sc.shortcode = r.shortcode GROUP BY 1,2), old_one AS (SELECT uid, day, min(sid) AS sid FROM old_fs GROUP BY 1,2), new_fs AS (SELECT study_id::string AS sid, user_id AS uid, min(timestamp)::date AS day FROM vlab.public.inference_data GROUP BY 1,2), new_one AS (SELECT uid, day, min(sid) AS sid FROM new_fs GROUP BY 1,2), pooled AS (SELECT * FROM old_one UNION ALL SELECT * FROM new_one), d AS (SELECT sid, day, count(*) AS n FROM pooled GROUP BY 1,2), q AS (SELECT * FROM d WHERE n >= 20), ps AS (SELECT sid, count(*) AS qdays, sum(n) AS recruited, percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY n::float8) AS med_day FROM q GROUP BY sid) SELECT count(*) AS studies, percentile_cont(0.10) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY med_day)::int AS p10, percentile_cont(0.25) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY med_day)::int AS p25, percentile_cont(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY med_day)::int AS median_study, percentile_cont(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY med_day)::int AS p75, percentile_cont(0.90) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY med_day)::int AS p90, max(med_day)::int AS mx, percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY qdays::float8)::int AS median_active_days, percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY recruited::float8)::int AS median_recruited FROM ps;
cockroach_quirk: count(DISTINCT x) returns a wrong value when it shares a SELECT list with percentile_cont(). Compute distinct counts in their own query.
